events.title: The martyrdom of St. Chrysogonus
events.shortBlurb: A Roman martyr whose name the Church still speaks in the Canon of the Mass was beheaded at Aquileia, tradition holds, in the persecution of Diocletian…
body: Chrysogonus, according to his ancient acts, was a Roman Christian and teacher, remembered in tradition as the instructor and support of St. Anastasia of Sirmium during the persecution. When the emperor demanded that all imprisoned Christians be brought to trial, he was taken from Rome to Aquileia in the north of Italy.

Summoned before the tribunal and commanded to sacrifice to the gods for the promise of honors, he answered that he would adore only the true God and that idols were but devils; for this, tradition says, he was beheaded on 24 November, about the year 304, and his body cast into the sea, to be recovered afterward and buried by a priest. The details of his passion are known only through his legendary acts and are held with caution.

His cult, however, is beyond doubt among the most ancient at Rome: his name was inserted into the Canon of the Mass, and a station church, San Crisogono in Trastevere, was raised in his honor. The Roman Martyrology keeps his memory on this day.
